children: , and other companies’ top executives are reportedly gaming out scenarios for a public and political revolt following a catastrophic artificial intelligence, or AI, event.
The executives are expecting large-scale events, including a cyberattack that could shut down access to internet connectivity, financial services, or even water and power, according to an
AI industry insiders told Axios they believe a major event will occur in the next six to 12 months.

The report highlighted that the first instance of harm caused by unsafe AI could turn a wary public further against the technology and its leaders, including Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, and President Trump, given his reluctance to regulate AI.
Many top AI executives and researchers believe that a major incident is inevitable.

According to the report, top AI players expect Democrats will move quickly to shut down AI. However, they will face significant challenges, as the global economy is intertwined with the buildout of AI infrastructure.

Additionally, many cybersecurity professionals believe that the proliferation of open-weight models, which can be downloaded and used to cause harm, means that such threats can be countered only by using AI.

Top AI executives believe that regulation has no chance of passing right now. However, they want to shape the policies and legislation that U.S. leaders could turn to after a first catastrophic event.
Even with Democrats in control of the House and Senate, the companies see fractured politics as the norm, including within the Democratic Party.
The report highlighted that some of the most heavy-handed Democratic proposals include banning superintelligence or pausing advanced AI development.

On the other hand, other proposals have bipartisan support and even some industry buy-in. These include requiring a kill switch for advanced AI. However, experts have questioned the viability of trying to turn off all AI systems.
In a real crisis, Washington can set partisan differences aside, according to the Axios report. One Democratic aide signaled cooperation during the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2008 financial crisis.

title: AI leaders prepare for worst-case scenario: Axios
